kept_features.summary: For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads.

method_verdict.method:
Adopt this method. For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the same strict-weak comparator select_detection already uses. highest_confidence orders by score, then area_px. largest_area orders by area_px, then score. source_index is not a key. A comparator that uses <= is not a strict weak ordering. std::max_element returns the first greatest element and replaces its champion only when that champion is strictly less than the next candidate, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. A tie is both keys equal. Under highest_confidence a later box with the same score and a larger area_px is strictly greater. Under largest_area the keys are reversed. NumPy argmax and Python max return that same first maximum. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty before the strategy check and before max_element, because an empty range returns last and must not be dereferenced. Any other strategy string throws std::invalid_argument and is not turned into a diagnostic.

Admission repeats that first maximum on the candidates not yet chosen, up to the count the caller passes, and stops at that count. admitted holds those winners in that rank order. One forward pass over the original vector appends every unchosen candidate to deferred, in candidate-list order. Each copied candidate keeps its source_index, the slot in this Detection2DArray, not Detection2D.id. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors. std::stable_sort preserves the relative order of equivalent elements, so its prefix can match that admitted order, but the tail of the sort is rank order and is not the deferred vector. std::partial_sort does not preserve the order of equivalent elements and leaves the unselected range in an unspecified order. std::stable_partition would keep the admitted side in input order, which is not rank order. A count of one admits the same candidate select_detection returns. A larger count than the list admits every candidate and leaves deferred empty.

The pose node calls select_stage2_subset with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 estimates that single admitted pallet and does not estimate deferred candidates. On success, PalletPoseStamped gains an int32 admitted_source_index and an int32[] deferred_source_indices after input_depth_stamp. Fields already on the message stay in place and stay filled. The pose header stamp stays the publish time. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps. ApproximateTime can match stamps that differ inside the configured interval, so the two lists are this pair only. An admitted index of 0 is a real detections slot. An empty deferred sequence means this pair had one class-matched candidate. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped stays a header and a pose.

When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped. The only result is the existing WARN DiagnosticStatus. Write the same two lists as two KeyValue entries on that status: admitted_source_index as decimal text, and deferred_source_indices as one comma-separated string in deferred order. One key holds one string, so a repeated key hides the list. Keep the status name, hardware id, WARN level, failure message, failure_reason, and both capture stamps. An empty deferred list is an empty string. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are: the empty-candidate return, and the depth-conversion return. An unknown detection_selection still throws rather than becoming a diagnostic.

Soft-NMS decays overlapping scores and can make a later box the next maximum; it does not leave every unselected candidate in input order. OpenCV NMS stable-sorts score and index so an equal score keeps the earlier index, then returns only the surviving indices. Weighted Boxes Fusion replaces a cluster with one confidence-weighted rectangle. DETR assigns a fixed query set with the Hungarian algorithm and drops non-maximum suppression. ByteTrack puts high-score boxes in one set and low-score boxes in another, associates the high set first, and deletes tracks that stay unmatched. ifm getPallet returns up to 10 pallets reordered by palletOrder, default scoreDescending, and palletIndex is a template type from 0 to 9. Isaac ROS FoundationPose builds the stage-2 mask from the highest-scoring detection. Detection2DArrayFilter replaces its running detection only when the score is strictly greater, so a tie keeps the earlier detection, and it publishes that one Detection2D without the detections it did not select. Lang2Lift selects the mask with the highest quality score and calls FoundationPose once. Wu and Demeester write a 6D pose for each detected pallet bin. Detection3D, PalletDetection, and PoseStamped have no deferred-index field. Detection2D.id may be empty and is an id across messages, not the slot in this array.

The rank is that linear first-maximum pass plus the walk that copies deferred. The cost that scales is one stage-2 estimate per admitted candidate. Classic chamfer measured 17.59 microseconds per hypothesis, oriented chamfer 51.50 microseconds, and directional chamfer 0.40 microseconds. CosyPose spent 190 ms of a 320 ms scene posing every candidate. Faster R-CNN region-wise time, including NMS, pooling, fully connected layers, and softmax, was 174 ms at about 2000 proposals and 47 ms at 300. A count of one stays at the single estimate, and each deferred source index is not another hypothesis. One int32 and a short int32[] sit in the payload range where ROS 2 end-to-end latency was equal from 128 bytes through 10 KB. REP-107's diagnostic channel is not a keepalive, and aggregation can leave it stale, so the success-path lists are on PalletPoseStamped. The failure path carries the same two lists on the one diagnostic that path publishes.

rejected_features.summary: Publish the pallet face width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped. Width and height are the spans of the plane inliers already built inside estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, along that estimate's plane axes. Depth is the mean z of those same inliers after the depth-to-RGB transform that already places the face centre. The handling process can then size the approach from this synchronized capture while the scene can still change.

For each stage-2 estimate, build the chamfer prototype from the width and height of the pallet face already recovered as plane inliers in that depth frame, instead of the fixed 1.20 m by 0.14 m factory face, so the template is the pallet the vehicle is about to handle.

For the detections in one capture, return which pallets are sent through stage 2 and which are deferred. select_stage2_subset ranks the existing DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements, admits at most the count this capture will pose, and places every remaining candidate in deferred. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred, and each candidate keeps its source_index. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet, and the other candidates in this array stay on the deferred vector for this capture. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The count is set for this capture because the scene can still change and stage 2 poses a subset of the array.

For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 the two class-matched pallet faces with the largest area_px, breaking remaining ties by higher score and then by lower source index, and mark every other candidate deferred. Each admitted face is passed to estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, and each success publishes its own PalletPoseStamped from that capture. Each deferred candidate is published as its source index together with this pair's RGB and depth stamps. A pair with fewer than two candidates admits every candidate and defers none. The handling process then has the poses of the large faces in this capture and the identities of the detections this pair did not pose, while the scene can still change.

For each successful call of estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, publish the pallet width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped. Width and height are the factory face that call already matches, params.pallet_width_m 1.20 m and params.pallet_height_m 0.14 m, and the search template stays that face. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose. Depth is the length of this pallet along the face normal on the side farther from the camera, through the two fork openings the prototype already cuts. Of the points sample_face_points already returned, keep those that, after the plane projection is translated by the opposite of best_pose's tx and ty and rotated by the opposite of the rotation rotate_proto_into applies, fall inside either pocket rectangle: centres at plus and minus pocket_centre_offset_m along the prototype width axis, with sides pocket_width_m and pocket_height_m. A point counts only when its signed point_to_plane_distance is less than the negation of plane_inlier_threshold_m. The camera-facing normal makes that negative side the side farther from the camera, and the point's contribution is the negation of that signed distance. depth_m is the median of those contributions. has_body_depth is true only when that set is non-empty. When the set is empty, has_body_depth is false, publish_pose still publishes the pose with the factory face width and height, and the handling process reads depth_m as a body length only when has_body_depth is true. The fields width_m, height_m, depth_m, and has_body_depth are written on the outcome and, after input_depth_stamp, on PalletPoseStamped. A failed estimate still publishes no PalletPoseStamped. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate select_detection already chooses. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes belong to this capture while the scene can still change. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that depth is the median far-side length through those two pocket openings, and that has_body_depth is false when the openings show no body.

survey_points: PalletPoseNode::on_pair keeps every class-matched candidate in a local vector through publish_pose and publish_failure_diagnostics, then that vector is destroyed. extract_detection_candidates walks the Detection2DArray once, keeps the highest-scoring hypothesis per detection, and stores source_index as that detection's slot (skipped non-matches leave gaps). select_detection is one std::max_element and returns that DetectionCandidate by value. Default strategy highest_confidence ranks score, then area_px; largest_area swaps that key order. A full tie keeps the earlier candidate because max_element returns the first maximum, so the later tied candidate stays in the vector with the other non-selected candidates. An unknown strategy throws. There is no subset split. Two early returns publish nothing: an empty candidate list, and a depth_image_to_meters exception. estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 runs once, and only that source_index is stored as PoseResult.instance_id or FailureResult.instance_id. publish_pose writes PalletPoseStamped with yaw, face normal, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, chamfer_cost_m, and this pair's input_rgb_stamp and input_depth_stamp (det_msg->header.stamp and depth_msg->header.stamp; ApproximateTime queue 10, slop 0.10 s). The message ends at input_depth_stamp and has no source-index fields. publish_ok_diagnostics emits chamfer_cost_m, plane_inlier_ratio, n_face_points, and those two stamps. On estimate failure the only publish is publish_failure_diagnostics (failure_reason plus those two stamps); instance_id is not written and no PalletPoseStamped is published. Detector postprocess caps the list at max_detections 10, so ranking it is a few comparisons. Writing the one admitted source index and the not-admitted source indexes, still in that candidate-list order, onto PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp, and the same two lists onto the failure diagnostic, is a few integers outside the chamfer loop. Calling estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 once per extra detection would repeat the 45700-evaluation search.

Measured stage-2 time is that single estimate. two_stage_chamfer_search_v2 always runs: free coarse is 21 x 31 x 31 = 20181 (±10 deg at 1 deg, ±0.15 m at 0.01 m) and free fine is 13 x 25 x 25 = 8125 (±1.2 deg at 0.2 deg, ±0.012 m at 0.001 m). two_stage_chamfer_search_v2_with_prior runs unless lambda_eff <= lambda_floor 0.05. confidence is clamp((0.020 - free_cost) / 0.014, 0, 1) and lambda_eff is prior_lambda 3.0 times (1 - confidence), so the prior is skipped only when free_cost is at or below 0.020 - 0.014 * (1 - 0.05/3) = 0.006233333333333334 m. The prior search is centered on the PCA init_pose, not on free_pose. Prior coarse is 21 x 21 x 21 = 9261 (±0.10 m at 0.01 m, same 21 yaw steps) plus another 8125 fine evaluations. The four grids are 45692 evaluations. Each of the four stage searches also evaluates its seed once before the parallel loop, and the zero-offset cell is inside the grid, so that seed is a second data cost. choose_pi_ambiguous_pose adds two full costs, the anchor chamfer_cost_v2 adds one and always runs before the lambda_eff branch, and a successful prior path adds one more data-only chamfer_cost_v2. The common frame when the prior runs is 45700 chamfer_cost_from_rotated evaluations. OpenMP schedule(static) splits that count across threads and does not drop evaluations; the critical section runs once per thread.

Each of those evaluations is O(N log N) with N=182. cached_prototype builds the default contour once and rebuilds it only when shape parameters change: 1.20 x 0.14 m outer face plus two 0.47 x 0.10 m pockets at contour_spacing_m 0.03, using n = max(2, ceil(length/spacing)+1) per edge with the endpoint omitted (94 + 44 + 44). rotate_proto_into writes the N x 2 rotation into thread-local ChamferTls.rotated once per theta (proto * R.transpose() only when theta changes). chamfer_cost_from_rotated still assigns tls.translated = rotated and adds tx, ty on every pose, sample_bilinear_into setConstant-fills the N distances then bilinear-samples all N, assign-copies them into tls.sorted, and std::sorts all N even though trim_fraction 0.10 sums only ceil(0.9*N) = 164. The bilinear reads are Eigen column-major points(i, 0) and points(i, 1), a stride of N doubles. At 45700 evaluations the translation copy is 133078400 bytes and the sort copy is 66539200 bytes, before the sort itself.

Before the grid, and only for the candidate select_detection already chose: depth_image_to_meters convertTo-copies the whole depth frame into a new CV_32FC1 once per synced pair (camera.yaml depth is 640x480; 16UC1 is scaled by depth_scale 0.001), so that copy does not multiply with deferred indexes. build_bbox_mask zero-fills a 1920x1080 mask and erodes it erode_px 2 times with a 3x3 kernel, even though only the bbox rectangle is set. sample_face_points scans every depth pixel, O(Hd*Wd) = 307200, with a K_inv ray, an SE(3) into RGB, and a lookup in that full mask; the bbox does not cull the depth loop. Accepted points go into per-thread std::vector<Eigen::Vector3d> buckets that together reserve Hd*Wd/4 (76800 Vector3d, about 1.8 MB) and are copied again, row by row, into points_depth_frame. ransac_plane_fit (up to ransac_iters 100, early stop at inlier ratio 0.85) allocates a residual array and a bool mask of length n_face_points every iteration, then copies inliers into a fresh matrix for JacobiSVD. plane_inlier_mask allocates those arrays again, and the pipeline copies the inliers a second time into plane_points_3d. project_points_to_plane_2d allocates an n_plane_inliers x 3 relative matrix and an n_plane_inliers x 2 result; PCA centres another n_plane_inliers x 2 copy. The distance image is built once per detection, not per pose. rasterize_points_to_mask uses resolution_m 0.005 and padding_m 0.80: a nominal 1.20 m by 0.14 m face is 561 by 350 (padded x span 2.8 m; padded y span 1.7400000000000002 m so ceil(span/0.005) is 349 and the +1 makes 350). close_mask clones the mask, runs a 5x5 elliptical MORPH_CLOSE (close_radius_px 2), then connectedComponentsWithStats and a second full-size mask. extract_boundary_mask erodes with a 3x3 kernel and builds another edge image. compute_distance_transform_v2 calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE and convertTo to CV_32FC1. The prototype cache does not reuse that distance image. These passes are smaller than the 45692-evaluation grid and would repeat for each extra posed detection.

Stage 1 is a separate process and is not where the admitted and deferred source indexes are published. rtdetr_detector_node defaults to backend mock, which skips inference copies. detector.yaml and full_pipeline.launch.py set backend tensorrt at input 640 with max_detections 10 and no NMS. On that path image_to_rgb copies msg.data via bytes() into a 1920x1080x3 array (about 6.2 MB; bgr8 reverses channels into a second array), preprocess resizes to 640x640 and builds a float32 CHW ascontiguousarray (1x3x640x640, about 4.9 MB), and TensorRTBackend.infer copies into pinned host memory, memcpy HtoD, execute_async_v3, memcpy DtoH, then copies labels, boxes, and scores back. That host traffic is upstream of the pair delivered to on_pair. The admission integers do not change it. geometry_core links Eigen3, OpenCV core/imgproc, yaml-cpp, and OpenMP; yaml-cpp loads the camera model only in the pose-node constructor, not per frame.
